primary_task: Given a GitHub issue URL, append an '#### Issues' block with the issue and its Linear key (taken from the linear-code comment on the issue) to the current PR description.

requirements.name: gh CLI
requirements.evidence: gh pr view --json number,body -q '.number'; gh issue view <n> --repo <owner>/<repo> --json comments; gh pr edit <pr-number> --body ...
requirements.basis: The user's GitHub account is usable through the github connector and through the gh CLI via the proxy.

requirements.name: grep/head/cat (shell utilities)
requirements.basis: bash: run shell commands on Linux x86_64

requirements.name: open PR for the current branch and the issue
requirements.evidence: If no PR exists on the branch, stop and tell the user.
requirements.basis: The manifest does not say; depends on the user's repo state (the github connector can look it up)

requirements.name: Linear account
requirements.evidence: Fetch the Linear ticket from the issue's linear-linkback comment (read from GitHub; Linear itself is never called)
requirements.basis: accounts, logins, API keys or credentials for external services other than the listed connectors and GitHub (cloud providers ..., SaaS products, ...)

notes: The Linear key is read from a GitHub comment authored by linear-code, so no Linear access is needed, and the doc allows asking the user or omitting the key. gh pr edit writes to GitHub; I treated it as covered by the GitHub account grant (the github connector exposes create_pull_request and issue_write). If forbid_effects writes_external were read to cover editing the PR body, the verdict would be BLOCKED.
